items.title: A call through a `dyn` object escapes the const-only check: the program checks clean, then throws `ReferenceError: __emit_asset is not defined` at run time (0.55.1 too)
items.discussion: found by lane ctx-58b (Order 58, 2026-11-13) beside B742; not caused by it: vilan 0.55.1 does the same; repro, outputs and a ready `#[ignore]`d pin in `scripts/integration/sweeps/order58/repros/b744-*`
items.body: `let erased: dyn Emitter = Token {}; erased.text()` where `Token::text` reaches `asset::emit` (compile-time-only): checks clean (exit 0), then the run fails with `ReferenceError: __emit_asset is not defined`. The control, the same program with a plain `Token {}` receiver, is refused at check (`text` (it reaches `asset::emit`) is compile-time-only). CAUSE (lane's reading): `refined_runtime_callers` names its dispatch sites through a local `dispatched_name` that reads only `async_infer::dispatch_at` (the `generic_dispatch` record); a call through a `dyn` object is recorded in `program.dyn_method_calls` instead, gets no name and is never listed as a site. The context pass names its sites through `dispatch_refine::member_name_at`, which checks `dyn_method_calls` first: that is why the context pass sees the call and the const-only check does not. FIX: one naming function for both passes; a `dyn` site charges every implementation of the member (no receiver is on record). Pin: `b744_a_dyn_objects_dispatch_into_an_emitting_impl_is_refused` in `inference/styling.rs` (text saved in the repros directory), plus a `dyn` object reached through a generic, a `dyn` in a field, and the case that must stay accepted (no implementation of the member emits). Check the native backend's answer for the same program.
